+# =============================================================================
+# evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml — cycle-130 Loa 2.0 component ablation suite
+#
+# SDD §3.3 (structure reproduced), extended by Sprint 258 Task 1.6: the
+# tasks block with the smoke root, phase_defaults, phase_sets, cost_hint, each
+# arm's phase-set override and took-effect rule ids, and the full pre-registered
+# rules block (D-A5; mirrored in NOTES before the first run, DEC-0383).
+#
+# Readers: execute-agent.sh / lib/sandbox-mount.sh (arms[].toggles via
+# resolve_arm_toggles), pipeline-run.sh (phase_defaults, phase_sets,
+# arms[].phases, arms[].effort), took-effect.sh (arms[].took_effect),
+# run-ablation.sh (trials, caps, priority, cut_ladder, arms[].task_types),
+# ablation-report.py (rules), validate-suite.sh (arm ids for the leakage check,
+# task_types against the known types).
+#
+# task_types: `all` | `build` (= feature-build, bug-fix, refactor) |
+#   `review-catch` | a single build type. An arm is never scheduled, and a row
+#   never reported, on a type outside its declaration (DEC-0400, DEC-0406).
+# took_effect: rule ids took-effect.sh evaluates per trial (DEC-0418); a miss is
+#   infrastructure_error and pauses the arm. `applicability_refused` is the
+#   smoke's evidence line that the planner refused the arm on a review-catch task.
+# =============================================================================
+name: ablation-2.0
+version: 1
+source_commit: "<sprint-258-commit>"   # the lead sets the Sprint 258 commit (rc.5 plus the mount fix; F2, DEC-0392)
+agy_opt_in: false
+tasks:
+  root: grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/tasks
+  manifest: grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/MANIFEST.sha256
+  smoke_root: grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/smoke
+suite_version: 1
+trials: {build: 3, review-catch: 3}      # D-A4: review-catch trials 3, not 5, under the gate pipeline
+cut_ladder: ["A5, A6, A7 not run", "A2 and A3 build trials 3 -> 2", "A3 review-catch trials 3 -> 2"]   # DEC-0397; A0, A1, A4 keep 3
+caps: {cycle_usd: 1500, run_usd: 12, reserve_usd: 250}   # reserve released to A7 when the re-verification rule needs no run (DEC-0398)
+priority: [a0_bare, a1_full, a2_no_sprint_plan, a3_one_voice, a4_no_gates, a7_effort_medium, a5_no_flatline, a6_one_window]
+cost_hint: {build: 7, review-catch: 8}   # USD per run before any actual exists (run-arms/run-ablation est_next fallback)
+
+# Session defaults per phase (SDD D-4.3). A6's continued session carries the
+# caps of the phase it is in; A0's BARE caps are PLAN + IMPLEMENT + 2 x FIX.
+phase_defaults:
+  models:
+    PLAN: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
+    IMPLEMENT: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
+    FIX: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
+    BARE: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
+    REVIEW: global.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1
+    AUDIT: global.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1
+  # REVIEW/AUDIT 60 turns / 30 min: the Sprint 258 smoke saw a review-catch AUDIT hit 40 turns after writing its
+  # verdict (DEC-0490); BARE stays the implementer-side sum (PLAN + IMPLEMENT + 2 x FIX)
+  max_turns: {PLAN: 30, IMPLEMENT: 60, REVIEW: 60, FIX: 40, AUDIT: 60, BARE: 170}
+  timeout_min: {PLAN: 15, IMPLEMENT: 25, REVIEW: 30, FIX: 15, AUDIT: 30, BARE: 70}
+  tools: "Bash,Read,Grep,Glob,Write,Edit,Task,WebFetch"   # identical for every arm, A0 included
+phase_sets:   # D-4.1: A1's phases per task type; FIX runs only after a CHANGES_REQUIRED gate
+  review-catch: [REVIEW, AUDIT]
+  build: [PLAN, IMPLEMENT, REVIEW, FIX, AUDIT, FIX]
+
+arms:
+  - {id: a0_bare, label: A0, task_types: [all], toggles: {loa_mount: false}, phases: [BARE], effort: high,
+     took_effect: [no_dot_claude, no_system_prompt, no_audit_rows, integrity_clean]}
+  - {id: a1_full, label: A1, task_types: [all], toggles: {}, took_effect: [all_phases_present, integrity_clean]}
+  - {id: a2_no_sprint_plan, label: A2, task_types: [build], toggles: {sprint_plan: false},
+     phases: [IMPLEMENT, REVIEW, FIX, AUDIT, FIX],
+     took_effect: [no_plan_phase, applicability_refused, integrity_clean]}
+  - {id: a3_one_voice, label: A3, task_types: [all], toggles: {companion_voice: false}, took_effect: [one_voice_planned, integrity_clean]}
+  - {id: a4_no_gates, label: A4, task_types: [build], toggles: {gates: false},
+     phases: [PLAN, IMPLEMENT],
+     took_effect: [no_gate_phases, enforce_env_false, applicability_refused, integrity_clean]}   # build only: on a review-catch task the gates are the task (DEC-0400)
+  - {id: a5_no_flatline, label: A5, task_types: [build], toggles: {flatline: false},
+     took_effect: [no_flatline_rows, applicability_refused, integrity_clean]}
+  - {id: a6_one_window, label: A6, task_types: [build], toggles: {context_resets: false},
+     took_effect: [implementer_single_session, gates_separate_sessions, applicability_refused, integrity_clean]}
+  - {id: a7_effort_medium, label: A7, task_types: [all], toggles: {effort: medium},
+     took_effect: [effort_flag_medium, skill_effort_stripped, integrity_clean]}
+  - {id: a8_no_ceremonies, label: A8, absent: true,
+     evidence: "no /meeting command, skill or sosyete config key at 4d69c3c4 (grep -rli sosyete .claude/ docs/; ls .claude/commands .claude/skills)"}
+
+rules:   # D-A5: pre-registered, mirrored in NOTES
+  threshold_points: 0.03
+  cost_lower_pct: 15
+  bootstrap: {resamples: 10000, level: 0.90, paired: true, units: {hidden_test_pass_rate: tasks, defect_catch_rate: defects}, also_report: {defect_catch_rate: tasks}}   # DEC-0399
+  primaries_by_arm: {build_only: [hidden_test_pass_rate], all_types: [hidden_test_pass_rate, defect_catch_rate]}   # DEC-0400
+  cap_failure: counts_as_failed            # 0 on each applicable primary (DEC-0393)
+  exclusion: {statuses: [degraded, contaminated, interrupted], mode: pairwise, inconclusive_above_share: 0.25}
+  sensitivity_figure: cap_failures_excluded  # printed, never decides
+  multiple_comparisons: none                 # expected false positives at 0.90 over 6 components printed
+  drift_guard: {cli_version: fixed_per_batch, model_ids: fixed_per_batch}   # DEC-0407
+  order: trial_major_seeded_shuffle_within_block
+  took_effect_per_trial: true                # a miss → infrastructure_error, arm paused until --clear-arm (DEC-0418)
+  predicates:                                # DEC-0416; d = arm − A1 point estimate, [lo, hi] its 90 % interval, c/w = cost/wall-clock Δ %
+    investigate: "any applicable primary has lo > 0"
+    keep: "else any applicable primary has d < -0.03 and hi < 0"
+    inconclusive: "else any applicable primary has d < -0.03, or the arm's excluded share > 0.25, or no valid pair"
+    remove: "else every applicable primary has d >= -0.03 and (c <= -15 or w <= -15)"
+    simplify: "else (every applicable primary within -0.03, cost similar)"
+  review_catch: {defect_counts_once_across_gates: true, false_positive_dedupe: cited_region, verdict_accurate_iff: "CHANGES_REQUIRED when the key holds a high or critical defect, APPROVED when none"}   # DEC-0420
+  inconclusive_extension_trials: 2
+  h1: "a1_full beats a0_bare on at least one primary with the interval excluding zero, else halt before promotion"
+  a4_sensitivity: "a4_no_gates worse than a1_full on hidden_test_pass_rate with the interval excluding zero, else harden tasks before acting on other arms"
+  decision_states: [investigate, keep, inconclusive, remove, simplify, not_run_cut, inconclusive_by_power]
+  mde_cut: 0.10   # sprint Task 3.4: an arm whose MDE at affordable trials exceeds this is pre-declared inconclusive_by_power and not run

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# validate-suite.sh — cycle-130 ablation task-suite validator (SDD §3.2, DEC-0424)
+#
+# Checks every task of the ablation-2.0 suite before it is frozen, run or graded.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   validate-suite.sh [--root DIR] [--smoke] [--allow-partial] [--suite-file F]
+#
+#   --root DIR        suite root (default grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0); the
+#                     tasks are <root>/tasks/<id>/task.yaml
+#   --smoke           also validate <root>/smoke/<id>/task.yaml (never counted)
+#   --allow-partial   skip the four-by-four type count (Sprint 258 state)
+#   --suite-file F    suite yaml (default evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml): arm ids
+#                     for the leakage check, arms' task_types, suite_version
+#
+# Checks (each violation is one stdout line `<task-id>: <reason>`):
+#   1. schema: id (= directory name), schema_version 1, type (feature-build |
+#      bug-fix | refactor | review-catch), source {kind, date, fix_commit?,
+#      base_commit?, bead?, origin?}, post_cutoff (bool), fixture (dir under the
+#      root; null only for review-catch), criterion (agent-facing; no path, file
+#      name or test name), success_criterion, test_command (array; null only for
+#      review-catch), regression_command (array | null), reference_patch (hidden/…
+#      | null; required for bug-fix and feature-build), grader_protected (array of
+#      relative paths present in the fixture), structural_check (hidden/… | null;
+#      required for refactor), bounds {max_turns{}, timeout_min{}} (phase → positive
+#      int), review_catch (null, or {fixture, manifest, labels?} for review-catch,
+#      both present), suite_version (= the suite file's), TASK.md present
+#   2. counts: four tasks of each type under tasks/ (unless --allow-partial)
+#   3. allowlist: test_command[0] and regression_command[0] in python3 | pytest |
+#      bats | bash | node | npx
+#   4. hidden/manifest.json (build types): {"files": [{src, dest}]}; every src
+#      exists under hidden/; every dest is relative, inside the tree, no `..`
+#   5. fixture path rule (build types): check_fixture_path_rule from
+#      lib/sandbox-mount.sh — no .claude/, CLAUDE.md, .loa.config.yaml, grimoires/
+#      or .run/ at the fixture's top level; the reference patch touches none either
+#   6. leakage: TASK.md and criterion (the task-brief text is built from these)
+#      and every phase prompt under evals/harness/lib/phase-prompts/ contain none
+#      of: the string `hidden` (any case), a hidden test file's stem, a defect id
+#      of the review manifest, a `D[0-9]{2}-` key, an arm id of the suite file
+#   7. suite file: every non-absent arm's task_types are known (all | build |
+#      review-catch | feature-build | bug-fix | refactor)
+#
+# Exit: 0 valid; 1 violations (every one listed); 2 usage / unreadable input.
+# Tested by evals/tests/validate-suite.bats.
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+export LC_ALL=C
+
+SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
+REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
+ROOT="$REPO_ROOT/grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0"
+SUITE_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml"
+PROMPTS_DIR="${LOA_EVAL_PHASE_PROMPTS_DIR:-$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/phase-prompts}"
+SMOKE=false ALLOW_PARTIAL=false
+
+usage() { sed -n '2,/^# =====.*$/p' "$0" | sed -n '2,45p' | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2; }
+die() { echo "validate-suite: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
+
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --root) ROOT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
+    --smoke) SMOKE=true; shift ;;
+    --allow-partial) ALLOW_PARTIAL=true; shift ;;
+    --suite-file) SUITE_FILE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
+    --help|-h) usage ;;
+    *) die "unknown option: $1 (see --help)" ;;
+  esac
+done
+[[ -n "$ROOT" && -d "$ROOT" ]] || die "suite root not found: ${ROOT:-<empty>}"
+ROOT="$(cd "$ROOT" && pwd)"
+[[ -f "$SUITE_FILE" ]] || die "suite file not found: $SUITE_FILE"
+for tool in yq jq python3; do command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "missing tool: $tool"; done
+# eval.yml trust boundary: a literal in-tree path, no variable on the source line
+pushd "$SCRIPT_DIR" >/dev/null
+# shellcheck source=lib/sandbox-mount.sh
+source ./lib/sandbox-mount.sh
+popd >/dev/null
+
+WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/validate-suite.XXXXXX")"
+trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
+yq -o=json '.' "$SUITE_FILE" > "$WORK/suite.json" 2>/dev/null || die "suite file is not valid YAML: $SUITE_FILE"
+
+# Collect task directories: tasks/* (counted) and smoke/* (with --smoke).
+: > "$WORK/tasks.tsv"
+for group in tasks smoke; do
+  [[ "$group" == "smoke" && "$SMOKE" != "true" ]] && continue
+  [[ -d "$ROOT/$group" ]] || continue
+  for d in "$ROOT/$group"/*/; do
+    [[ -d "$d" ]] || continue
+    d="${d%/}"
+    n="$(basename "$d")"
+    j="$WORK/$group.$n.json"
+    if [[ ! -f "$d/task.yaml" ]]; then
+      printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$group" "$n" "$d" "-" >> "$WORK/tasks.tsv"; continue
+    fi
+    if yq -o=json '.' "$d/task.yaml" > "$j" 2>/dev/null && jq -e 'type == "object"' "$j" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$group" "$n" "$d" "$j" >> "$WORK/tasks.tsv"
+    else
+      printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$group" "$n" "$d" "!" >> "$WORK/tasks.tsv"
+    fi
+  done
+done
+
+# Python does the schema, counts, allowlist, manifest, leakage and suite checks;
+# it prints violations, and `FIXTURE\t<id>\t<dir>` lines for the path rule below.
+python3 -I - "$WORK/tasks.tsv" "$WORK/suite.json" "$ROOT" "$REPO_ROOT" "$ALLOW_PARTIAL" "$PROMPTS_DIR" > "$WORK/out.txt" <<'PY' || { cat "$WORK/out.txt" >&2 2>/dev/null; die "validator crashed"; }
+import json, os, re, sys
+
+tasks_tsv, suite_json, root, repo, allow_partial, prompts_dir = sys.argv[1:7]
+allow_partial = allow_partial == "true"
+suite = json.load(open(suite_json))
+out = []
+def bad(tid, msg): out.append(f"{tid}: {msg}")
+
+TYPES = ["feature-build", "bug-fix", "refactor", "review-catch"]
+BUILD = {"feature-build", "bug-fix", "refactor"}
+ALLOW = {"python3", "pytest", "bats", "bash", "node", "npx"}
+KNOWN_TASK_TYPES = {"all", "build", "review-catch", "feature-build", "bug-fix", "refactor"}
+MOUNT_OWNED = (".claude", "CLAUDE.md", ".loa.config.yaml", "grimoires", ".run")
+REQUIRED = ["id", "schema_version", "type", "source", "post_cutoff", "fixture", "criterion",
+            "success_criterion", "test_command", "regression_command", "reference_patch",
+            "grader_protected", "structural_check", "bounds", "review_catch", "suite_version"]
+
+arms = [a for a in (suite.get("arms") or []) if isinstance(a, dict)]
+arm_ids = sorted({a.get("id") for a in arms if isinstance(a.get("id"), str)})
+for a in arms:
+    if a.get("absent") is True:
+        continue
+    tt = a.get("task_types")
+    if not isinstance(tt, list) or not tt:
+        bad("suite", f"arm {a.get('id')} has no task_types list")
+        continue
+    for t in tt:
+        if t not in KNOWN_TASK_TYPES:
+            bad("suite", f"arm {a.get('id')} task_types names unknown type '{t}'")
+suite_version = suite.get("suite_version")
+
+def rel_ok(p):
+    return isinstance(p, str) and p and not p.startswith("/") and ".." not in p.split("/") and "\\" not in p
+
+def is_str_list(v):
+    return isinstance(v, list) and all(isinstance(x, str) and x for x in v)
+
+def read(p):
+    try:
+        return open(p, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
+    except OSError:
+        return None
+
+prompt_texts = []
+if os.path.isdir(prompts_dir):
+    for f in sorted(os.listdir(prompts_dir)):
+        if f.endswith(".md"):
+            prompt_texts.append((f"phase-prompts/{f}", read(os.path.join(prompts_dir, f)) or ""))
+
+def leak_scan(tid, label, text, stems, defect_ids):
+    low = text.lower()
+    if "hidden" in low:
+        bad(tid, f"leak: {label} contains the string 'hidden'")
+    for s in stems:
+        if s and re.search(r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])" + re.escape(s.lower()) + r"(?![A-Za-z0-9_])", low):
+            bad(tid, f"leak: {label} names the grader file stem '{s}'")
+    for d in defect_ids:
+        if d in text:
+            bad(tid, f"leak: {label} names defect id '{d}'")
+    m = re.search(r"\bD[0-9]{2}-", text)
+    if m:
+        bad(tid, f"leak: {label} carries a defect key pattern '{m.group(0)}'")
+    for a in arm_ids:
+        if re.search(r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])" + re.escape(a) + r"(?![A-Za-z0-9_])", text):
+            bad(tid, f"leak: {label} names arm id '{a}'")
+
+counts = {t: 0 for t in TYPES}
+seen = {}
+for line in open(tasks_tsv, encoding="utf-8"):
+    line = line.rstrip("\n")
+    if not line:
+        continue
+    group, name, tdir, jpath = line.split("\t")
+    tid = f"{group}/{name}"
+    if jpath == "-":
+        bad(tid, "no task.yaml"); continue
+    if jpath == "!":
+        bad(tid, "task.yaml is not a YAML mapping"); continue
+    t = json.load(open(jpath))
+    for k in REQUIRED:
+        if k not in t:
+            bad(tid, f"schema: missing field '{k}'")
+    if t.get("id") != name:
+        bad(tid, f"schema: id '{t.get('id')}' differs from the directory name")
+    if not isinstance(t.get("id"), str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}", t.get("id") or ""):
+        bad(tid, "schema: id must match [a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}")
+    elif t["id"] in seen:
+        bad(tid, f"schema: duplicate id (also {seen[t['id']]})")
+    else:
+        seen[t["id"]] = tid
+    if t.get("schema_version") != 1:
+        bad(tid, "schema: schema_version must be 1")
+    ttype = t.get("type")
+    if ttype not in TYPES:
+        bad(tid, f"schema: type '{ttype}' not in {'|'.join(TYPES)}")
+    elif group == "tasks":
+        counts[ttype] += 1
+    src = t.get("source")
+    if not isinstance(src, dict):
+        bad(tid, "schema: source must be a mapping")
+    else:
+        if not isinstance(src.get("kind"), str) or not src.get("kind"):
+            bad(tid, "schema: source.kind must be a non-empty string")
+        if not isinstance(src.get("date"), str) or not re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", src.get("date") or ""):
+            bad(tid, "schema: source.date must be YYYY-MM-DD")
+        for k in ("fix_commit", "base_commit"):
+            if k in src and src[k] is not None and not (isinstance(src[k], str) and re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{7,40}", src[k])):
+                bad(tid, f"schema: source.{k} must be a hex commit id")
+        for k in src:
+            if k not in ("kind", "date", "fix_commit", "base_commit", "bead", "origin"):
+                bad(tid, f"schema: source.{k} is not a known key")
+    if not isinstance(t.get("post_cutoff"), bool):
+        bad(tid, "schema: post_cutoff must be a boolean")
+    build = ttype in BUILD
+    fx = t.get("fixture")
+    fixture_dir = None
+    if fx is None:
+        if build:
+            bad(tid, "schema: fixture is required for build types")
+    elif not rel_ok(fx):
+        bad(tid, "schema: fixture must be a relative path inside the root")
+    elif not os.path.isdir(os.path.join(root, fx)):
+        bad(tid, f"schema: fixture directory not found: {fx}")
+    else:
+        fixture_dir = os.path.join(root, fx)
+        if build:
+            print(f"FIXTURE\t{tid}\t{fixture_dir}")
+    crit = t.get("criterion")
+    if not isinstance(crit, str) or not crit.strip():
+        bad(tid, "schema: criterion must be a non-empty string")
+        crit = ""
+    else:
+        if "/" in crit or re.search(r"\b[\w.-]+\.(py|sh|bats|js|ts|mjs|json|ya?ml|md|toml|cfg|ini|txt|patch)\b", crit):
+            bad(tid, "schema: criterion names a path or file (agent-facing behaviour only)")
+        if re.search(r"\btest_\w+", crit):
+            bad(tid, "schema: criterion names a test")
+    if not isinstance(t.get("success_criterion"), str) or not t.get("success_criterion", "").strip():
+        bad(tid, "schema: success_criterion must be a non-empty string")
+    for key in ("test_command", "regression_command"):
+        v = t.get(key)
+        if v is None:
+            if key == "test_command" and ttype != "review-catch":
+                bad(tid, "schema: test_command is required for build types")
+            continue
+        if not is_str_list(v) or not v:
+            bad(tid, f"schema: {key} must be a non-empty array of strings or null")
+        elif v[0] not in ALLOW:
+            bad(tid, f"allowlist: {key}[0] '{v[0]}' not in {'|'.join(sorted(ALLOW))}")
+    for key, must in (("reference_patch", ttype in ("bug-fix", "feature-build")), ("structural_check", ttype == "refactor")):
+        v = t.get(key)
+        if v is None:
+            if must:
+                bad(tid, f"schema: {key} is required for {ttype}")
+            continue
+        if not rel_ok(v) or not v.startswith("hidden/"):
+            bad(tid, f"schema: {key} must be a relative path under hidden/")
+        elif not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(tdir, v)):
+            bad(tid, f"schema: {key} not found: {v}")
+    gp = t.get("grader_protected")
+    if not isinstance(gp, list) or not all(isinstance(x, str) for x in gp):
+        bad(tid, "schema: grader_protected must be an array of paths")
+    else:
+        for p in gp:
+            if not rel_ok(p):
+                bad(tid, f"schema: grader_protected path '{p}' is not a relative path inside the tree")
+            elif fixture_dir and not os.path.exists(os.path.join(fixture_dir, p)):
+                bad(tid, f"schema: grader_protected path '{p}' is not in the fixture")
+    bounds = t.get("bounds")
+    if not isinstance(bounds, dict) or set(bounds) != {"max_turns", "timeout_min"}:
+        bad(tid, "schema: bounds must be {max_turns: {}, timeout_min: {}}")
+    else:
+        for k in ("max_turns", "timeout_min"):
+            m = bounds[k]
+            if not isinstance(m, dict) or not all(isinstance(x, int) and not isinstance(x, bool) and x > 0 for x in m.values()):
+                bad(tid, f"schema: bounds.{k} must map phases to positive integers")
+            elif any(p not in ("PLAN", "IMPLEMENT", "REVIEW", "FIX", "AUDIT", "BARE") for p in m):
+                bad(tid, f"schema: bounds.{k} names an unknown phase")
+    rc = t.get("review_catch")
+    defect_ids = []
+    if ttype == "review-catch":
+        if not isinstance(rc, dict):
+            bad(tid, "schema: review_catch {fixture, manifest} is required for review-catch")
+        else:
+            for k in rc:
+                if k not in ("fixture", "manifest", "labels"):
+                    bad(tid, f"schema: review_catch.{k} is not a known key")
+            rf, rm = rc.get("fixture"), rc.get("manifest")
+            if not rel_ok(rf) or not os.path.isdir(os.path.join(repo, "evals", "fixtures", rf)):
+                bad(tid, f"schema: review_catch.fixture not found under evals/fixtures: {rf}")
+            if not rel_ok(rm) or not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(repo, rm)):
+                bad(tid, f"schema: review_catch.manifest not found: {rm}")
+            else:
+                try:
+                    defect_ids = [d.get("id") for d in json.load(open(os.path.join(repo, rm))).get("defects", []) if d.get("id")]
+                except (OSError, ValueError, AttributeError):
+                    bad(tid, f"schema: review_catch.manifest is not a defect manifest: {rm}")
+    elif rc is not None:
+        bad(tid, "schema: review_catch must be null for build types")
+    sv = t.get("suite_version")
+    if not isinstance(sv, int) or isinstance(sv, bool) or sv < 1:
+        bad(tid, "schema: suite_version must be a positive integer")
+    elif suite_version is not None and sv != suite_version:
+        bad(tid, f"schema: suite_version {sv} differs from the suite file's {suite_version}")
+
+    stems = []
+    hm = os.path.join(tdir, "hidden", "manifest.json")
+    if build:
+        if not os.path.isfile(hm):
+            bad(tid, "hidden: hidden/manifest.json is missing")
+        else:
+            try:
+                files = json.load(open(hm)).get("files")
+            except (OSError, ValueError, AttributeError):
+                files = None
+            if not isinstance(files, list) or not files:
+                bad(tid, "hidden: manifest.json must be {\"files\": [{src, dest}, ...]}")
+            else:
+                for e in files:
+                    s_, d_ = (e or {}).get("src"), (e or {}).get("dest")
+                    if not rel_ok(s_) or not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(tdir, "hidden", s_)):
+                        bad(tid, f"hidden: manifest src not found under hidden/: {s_}")
+                    if not rel_ok(d_):
+                        bad(tid, f"hidden: manifest dest must be a relative path inside the tree: {d_}")
+                    elif d_.split("/")[0] in MOUNT_OWNED:
+                        bad(tid, f"hidden: manifest dest lands on a mount-owned path: {d_}")
+                    if isinstance(s_, str) and s_:
+                        stems.append(os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(s_))[0])
+        sc = t.get("structural_check")
+        if isinstance(sc, str) and sc:
+            stems.append(os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(sc))[0])
+        rp = t.get("reference_patch")
+        if isinstance(rp, str) and os.path.isfile(os.path.join(tdir, rp)):
+            for pl in (read(os.path.join(tdir, rp)) or "").splitlines():
+                m = re.match(r"^(?:\+\+\+|---) (?:[ab]/)?(\S+)", pl)
+                if m and m.group(1) != "/dev/null" and m.group(1).split("/")[0] in MOUNT_OWNED:
+                    bad(tid, f"fixture path rule: reference patch touches a mount-owned path: {m.group(1)}")
+    task_md = read(os.path.join(tdir, "TASK.md"))
+    if task_md is None:
+        bad(tid, "schema: TASK.md is missing")
+        task_md = ""
+    leak_scan(tid, "TASK.md", task_md, stems, defect_ids)
+    leak_scan(tid, "criterion", crit, stems, defect_ids)
+    for label, text in prompt_texts:
+        leak_scan(tid, label, text, stems, defect_ids)
+
+if not allow_partial:
+    for ty in TYPES:
+        if counts[ty] != 4:
+            bad("suite", f"counts: {counts[ty]} {ty} task(s) under tasks/, want 4 (pass --allow-partial before the freeze)")
+
+for o in out:
+    print(o)
+PY
+
+violations=0
+: > "$WORK/report.txt"
+while IFS= read -r line; do
+  if [[ "$line" == FIXTURE$'\t'* ]]; then
+    IFS=$'\t' read -r _ tid fdir <<<"$line"
+    if ! check_fixture_path_rule "$fdir" 2>"$WORK/rule.err"; then
+      printf '%s: fixture path rule: %s\n' "$tid" "$(tr '\n' ' ' < "$WORK/rule.err" | sed 's/ *$//')" >> "$WORK/report.txt"
+    fi
+  else
+    printf '%s\n' "$line" >> "$WORK/report.txt"
+  fi
+done < "$WORK/out.txt"
+violations="$(grep -c . "$WORK/report.txt" || true)"
+ntasks="$(grep -c . "$WORK/tasks.tsv" || true)"
+if [[ "$violations" -gt 0 ]]; then
+  cat "$WORK/report.txt"
+  echo "validate-suite: $violations violation(s) over $ntasks task(s) in $ROOT" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+echo "validate-suite: OK — $ntasks task(s) valid in $ROOT$([[ "$ALLOW_PARTIAL" == "true" ]] && echo " (partial: type counts not enforced)")"
+exit 0

+# =============================================================================
+# evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml — cycle-130 Loa 2.0 component ablation suite
+#
+# SDD §3.3 (structure reproduced), extended by Sprint 258 Task 1.6: the
+# tasks block with the smoke root, phase_defaults, phase_sets, cost_hint, each
+# arm's phase-set override and took-effect rule ids, and the full pre-registered
+# rules block (D-A5; mirrored in NOTES before the first run, DEC-0383).
+#
+# Readers: execute-agent.sh / lib/sandbox-mount.sh (arms[].toggles via
+# resolve_arm_toggles), pipeline-run.sh (phase_defaults, phase_sets,
+# arms[].phases, arms[].effort), took-effect.sh (arms[].took_effect),
+# run-ablation.sh (trials, caps, priority, cut_ladder, arms[].task_types),
+# ablation-report.py (rules), validate-suite.sh (arm ids for the leakage check,
+# task_types against the known types).
+#
+# task_types: `all` | `build` (= feature-build, bug-fix, refactor) |
+#   `review-catch` | a single build type. An arm is never scheduled, and a row
+#   never reported, on a type outside its declaration (DEC-0400, DEC-0406).
+# took_effect: rule ids took-effect.sh evaluates per trial (DEC-0418); a miss is
+#   infrastructure_error and pauses the arm. `applicability_refused` is the
+#   smoke's evidence line that the planner refused the arm on a review-catch task.
+# =============================================================================
+name: ablation-2.0
+version: 1
+source_commit: "<sprint-258-commit>"   # the lead sets the Sprint 258 commit (rc.5 plus the mount fix; F2, DEC-0392)
+agy_opt_in: false
+tasks:
+  root: grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/tasks
+  manifest: grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/MANIFEST.sha256
+  smoke_root: grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/smoke
+suite_version: 1
+trials: {build: 3, review-catch: 3}      # D-A4: review-catch trials 3, not 5, under the gate pipeline
+cut_ladder: ["A5, A6, A7 not run", "A2 and A3 build trials 3 -> 2", "A3 review-catch trials 3 -> 2"]   # DEC-0397; A0, A1, A4 keep 3
+caps: {cycle_usd: 1500, run_usd: 12, reserve_usd: 250}   # reserve released to A7 when the re-verification rule needs no run (DEC-0398)
+priority: [a0_bare, a1_full, a2_no_sprint_plan, a3_one_voice, a4_no_gates, a7_effort_medium, a5_no_flatline, a6_one_window]
+cost_hint: {build: 7, review-catch: 8}   # USD per run before any actual exists (run-arms/run-ablation est_next fallback)
+
+# Session defaults per phase (SDD D-4.3). A6's continued session carries the
+# caps of the phase it is in; A0's BARE caps are PLAN + IMPLEMENT + 2 x FIX.
+phase_defaults:
+  models:
+    PLAN: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
+    IMPLEMENT: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
+    FIX: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
+    BARE: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5

@@ -0,0 +1,136 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# tools/check-manifest-paths.sh — cycle-130 FR-1 (#1267; SDD §5.2, DEC-0368)
+#
+# CI gate for the System Zone integrity manifest: every path listed in
+# `.claude/checksums.json` must be TRACKED (`git ls-files -- .claude`) and
+# PRESENT in the working tree. A manifest generated by walking a dirty tree
+# (the #1267 class) lists build, cache and runtime artefacts that no fresh
+# mount has, so every downstream `check-loa.sh` reports them as Missing.
+#
+# Offenders are grouped on stderr:
+#   untracked  — listed in the manifest, not in `git ls-files`; each carries a
+#                DIAGNOSTIC class (first match wins):
+#                  __pycache__ | .pytest_cache | node_modules | .run
+#                      (a path component of that name)
+#                  .pyc   (name ends in .pyc)
+#                  .lock  (name ends in .lock)
+#                  other
+#   missing    — tracked, but absent from the working tree
+# The classes label untracked offenders only: a TRACKED path is never flagged
+# for its name (a committed `.lock` fixture is legitimate).
+#
+# Last line on stdout:
+#   manifest-paths: N entries, M untracked (class=count, ...), K missing
+#
+# Usage:
+#   tools/check-manifest-paths.sh [--manifest FILE] [--root DIR]
+#
+# Options:
+#   --root DIR       repository work tree (default: the git top level of the
+#                    current directory)
+#   --manifest FILE  manifest to check (default: ROOT/.claude/checksums.json)
+#   -h, --help       this text
+#
+# Exit codes:
+#   0  every manifest path is tracked and present
+#   1  at least one untracked or missing path (listed on stderr)
+#   2  usage error, ROOT is not a git work tree, or the manifest is absent or
+#      not JSON with a `files` object
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+export LC_ALL=C
+
+usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# =====/p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed -e '$d' -e 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
+die2() { echo "check-manifest-paths: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
+
+ROOT=""
+MANIFEST=""
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --root)
+      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--root requires a directory"
+      ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --manifest)
+      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--manifest requires a file path"
+      MANIFEST="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
+    *) die2 "unknown argument: $1 (see --help)" ;;
+  esac
+done
+
+if [[ -z "$ROOT" ]]; then
+  ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die2 "not inside a git work tree (use --root DIR)"
+fi
+[[ -d "$ROOT" ]] || die2 "--root is not a directory: $ROOT"
+ROOT="$(cd "$ROOT" && pwd -P)"
+[[ "$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree 2>/dev/null || true)" == "true" ]] \
+  || die2 "not a git work tree: $ROOT"
+[[ -n "$MANIFEST" ]] || MANIFEST="${ROOT}/.claude/checksums.json"
+[[ -f "$MANIFEST" ]] || die2 "manifest not found: $MANIFEST"
+jq -e '.files | type == "object"' "$MANIFEST" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
+  || die2 "manifest is not JSON with a files object: $MANIFEST"
+
+TMP_DIR="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/check-manifest-paths.XXXXXX")"
+cleanup() { rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"; }
+trap cleanup EXIT
+
+# Both lists newline-separated and C-sorted. A path with a newline cannot be
+# represented in either list; gen-checksums.sh refuses to emit one.
+git -C "$ROOT" ls-files -- .claude | sort -u > "${TMP_DIR}/tracked"
+jq -r '.files | keys[]' "$MANIFEST" | sort -u > "${TMP_DIR}/listed"
+comm -23 "${TMP_DIR}/listed" "${TMP_DIR}/tracked" > "${TMP_DIR}/untracked"
+comm -12 "${TMP_DIR}/listed" "${TMP_DIR}/tracked" > "${TMP_DIR}/both"
+
+classify() {
+  local p="$1"
+  if [[ "$p" =~ (^|/)(__pycache__|\.pytest_cache|node_modules|\.run)(/|$) ]]; then
+    printf '%s' "${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
+  elif [[ "$p" == *.pyc ]]; then
+    printf '.pyc'
+  elif [[ "$p" == *.lock ]]; then
+    printf '.lock'
+  else
+    printf 'other'
+  fi
+}
+
+# Classified untracked offenders: "<class>\t<path>"
+: > "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls"
+while IFS= read -r p; do
+  [[ -n "$p" ]] || continue
+  printf '%s\t%s\n' "$(classify "$p")" "$p" >> "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls"
+done < "${TMP_DIR}/untracked"
+
+: > "${TMP_DIR}/missing"
+while IFS= read -r p; do
+  [[ -n "$p" ]] || continue
+  [[ -e "${ROOT}/${p}" ]] || printf '%s\n' "$p" >> "${TMP_DIR}/missing"
+done < "${TMP_DIR}/both"
+
+entries=$(wc -l < "${TMP_DIR}/listed" | tr -d ' ')
+n_untracked=$(wc -l < "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls" | tr -d ' ')
+n_missing=$(wc -l < "${TMP_DIR}/missing" | tr -d ' ')
+
+class_summary=""
+if [[ "$n_untracked" -gt 0 ]]; then
+  echo "check-manifest-paths: untracked manifest paths (not in git ls-files -- .claude), by class:" >&2
+  for cls in __pycache__ .pytest_cache node_modules .run .pyc .lock other; do
+    c=$(awk -F'\t' -v c="$cls" '$1 == c' "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
+    [[ "$c" -gt 0 ]] || continue
+    class_summary="${class_summary:+${class_summary}, }${cls}=${c}"
+    echo "  [${cls}] ${c} path(s):" >&2
+    awk -F'\t' -v c="$cls" '$1 == c { print "    " $2 }' "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls" >&2
+  done
+fi
+if [[ "$n_missing" -gt 0 ]]; then
+  echo "check-manifest-paths: tracked manifest paths absent from the working tree:" >&2
+  sed 's/^/    /' "${TMP_DIR}/missing" >&2
+fi
+
+echo "manifest-paths: ${entries} entries, ${n_untracked} untracked${class_summary:+ (${class_summary})}, ${n_missing} missing"
+if [[ "$n_untracked" -gt 0 || "$n_missing" -gt 0 ]]; then
+  echo "check-manifest-paths: FAIL — regenerate with: bash tools/gen-checksums.sh" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+exit 0

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh — cycle-130 FR-1 (#1267; SDD §5.4, AC-1.3)
+#
+# Proves that a FRESH downstream submodule mount of this repository passes
+# `check-loa.sh` integrity: no Tampered, no Missing (paths the mount does not
+# link by design are reported as not-mounted and do not fail).
+#
+# Steps, all inside a new temp directory (nothing outside it is written):
+#   1. upstream/   — a `git clone` of this repository over file://, with a
+#                    local branch `fresh-mount-proof` at REF. With --worktree
+#                    the source work tree's uncommitted state (tracked edits,
+#                    deletions and untracked non-ignored files) is copied in
+#                    and committed on that branch, inside the temp clone only.
+#   2. downstream/ — `git init`, one commit, then the downstream entry point
+#                    `upstream/.claude/scripts/mount-submodule.sh --branch
+#                    fresh-mount-proof --ref <sha> --force` with
+#                    LOA_UPSTREAM=file://.../upstream (the mount clones the
+#                    submodule from there; no network).
+#   3. `aleph.enabled: false` is set in downstream/.loa.config.yaml.
+#   4. `bash .claude/scripts/check-loa.sh` runs in downstream/; its full output
+#      is printed, then a summary line
+#        fresh-mount-proof: Tampered=T Missing=M not-mounted=N check-loa-rc=R
+#
+# Git runs hermetically: GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1,
+# a fixed identity, protocol.file.allow=always (needed for a file:// submodule
+# on git >= 2.38.1) and core.hooksPath pointed at an empty directory.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh [--ref REF] [--worktree] [--keep] [--tmp DIR]
+#
+# Options:
+#   --ref REF    commit-ish of this repository to mount (default: HEAD of the
+#                repository the script lives in)
+#   --worktree   mount REF plus the source work tree's uncommitted state
+#                (use before the change is committed)
+#   --keep       keep the temp directory and print its path
+#   --tmp DIR    parent directory for the temp directory (default: $TMPDIR or
+#                /tmp)
+#   -h, --help   this text
+#
+# Exit codes:
+#   0    check-loa.sh exited 0 on the fresh mount
+#   1    check-loa.sh exited non-zero (its output names the failures)
+#   2    usage error
+#   3    setup failed (clone, overlay, downstream init or the mount itself);
+#        the failing step's output is printed
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+export LC_ALL=C
+
+usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# =====/p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed -e '$d' -e 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
+die2() { echo "fresh-mount-proof: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
+die3() { echo "fresh-mount-proof: SETUP FAILED: $*" >&2; exit 3; }
+
+REF=""
+KEEP=0
+WORKTREE=0
+TMP_PARENT="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}"
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --ref)
+      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--ref requires a commit-ish"
+      REF="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --tmp)
+      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--tmp requires a directory"
+      TMP_PARENT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --keep) KEEP=1; shift ;;
+    --worktree) WORKTREE=1; shift ;;
+    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
+    *) die2 "unknown argument: $1 (see --help)" ;;
+  esac
+done
+[[ -d "$TMP_PARENT" ]] || die2 "--tmp is not a directory: $TMP_PARENT"
+
+SELF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd -P)"
+SRC="$(git -C "$SELF_DIR" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die2 "script is not inside a git work tree"
+[[ -n "$REF" ]] || REF="HEAD"
+REF_SHA="$(git -C "$SRC" rev-parse --verify --quiet "${REF}^{commit}")" || die2 "not a commit in $SRC: $REF"
+
+WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMP_PARENT%/}/fresh-mount-proof.XXXXXX")"
+cleanup() {
+  if [[ $KEEP -eq 1 ]]; then
+    echo "fresh-mount-proof: kept $WORK" >&2
+  else
+    rm -rf "$WORK"
+  fi
+}
+trap cleanup EXIT
+
+# --- hermetic git ---------------------------------------------------------------
+mkdir -p "$WORK/no-hooks"
+export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1
+export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=3
+export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=protocol.file.allow GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=always
+export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1=core.hooksPath GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1="$WORK/no-hooks"
+export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_2=init.defaultBranch GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_2=main
+export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="fresh-mount-proof" GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="fresh-mount-proof@localhost"
+export GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="$GIT_AUTHOR_NAME" GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="$GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL"
+unset LOA_ALEPH_ENABLED
+
+LOG="$WORK/step.log"
+run_step() {  # run_step <description> <cmd...>; output to $LOG, printed on failure
+  local desc="$1"; shift
+  if ! "$@" > "$LOG" 2>&1; then
+    cat "$LOG" >&2
+    die3 "$desc"
+  fi
+}
+
+suffix=""
+[[ $WORKTREE -eq 1 ]] && suffix=" + work-tree state"
+echo "fresh-mount-proof: source $SRC at ${REF_SHA}${suffix}"
+echo "fresh-mount-proof: temp dir $WORK"
+
+# --- 1. upstream clone ----------------------------------------------------------
+UP="$WORK/upstream"
+run_step "clone $SRC" git clone --quiet --no-checkout "file://$SRC" "$UP"
+run_step "fetch $REF_SHA" git -C "$UP" fetch --quiet origin "$REF_SHA"
+run_step "branch at $REF_SHA" git -C "$UP" checkout --quiet -B fresh-mount-proof "$REF_SHA"
+
+overlay() {
+  local p
+  while IFS= read -r -d '' p; do
+    if [[ -e "$SRC/$p" || -L "$SRC/$p" ]]; then
+      [[ -d "$SRC/$p" && ! -L "$SRC/$p" ]] && continue   # gitlink / nested repo
+      mkdir -p "$UP/$(dirname "$p")"
+      rm -f "$UP/$p"
+      cp -P "$SRC/$p" "$UP/$p"
+    else
+      rm -f "$UP/$p"
+    fi
+  done < <(git -C "$SRC" ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard)
+  git -C "$UP" add -A
+  git -C "$UP" commit --quiet --allow-empty -m "fresh-mount-proof: work-tree state of $SRC"
+}
+[[ $WORKTREE -eq 1 ]] && run_step "work-tree overlay" overlay
+MOUNT_SHA="$(git -C "$UP" rev-parse HEAD)"
+echo "fresh-mount-proof: mounting upstream commit $MOUNT_SHA"
+
+# --- 2. downstream repository and the submodule mount --------------------------
+DOWN="$WORK/downstream"
+mkdir -p "$DOWN"
+init_downstream() {
+  git -C "$DOWN" init --quiet
+  printf '# downstream fixture\n' > "$DOWN/README.md"
+  git -C "$DOWN" add README.md
+  git -C "$DOWN" commit --quiet -m "initial commit"
+}
+run_step "downstream init" init_downstream
+
+do_mount() {
+  (cd "$DOWN" && LOA_UPSTREAM="file://$UP" bash "$UP/.claude/scripts/mount-submodule.sh" \
+    --branch fresh-mount-proof --ref "$MOUNT_SHA" --force < /dev/null)
+}
+run_step "mount-submodule.sh" do_mount
+echo "fresh-mount-proof: mount-submodule.sh exited 0 ($(grep -c 'Linked' "$LOG" || true) link lines)"
+
+# --- 3. Aleph off ---------------------------------------------------------------
+CFG="$DOWN/.loa.config.yaml"
+[[ -f "$CFG" ]] || : > "$CFG"
+if command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  run_step "aleph.enabled: false" yq -i '.aleph.enabled = false' "$CFG"
+else
+  printf '\naleph:\n  enabled: false\n' >> "$CFG"
+fi
+
+# --- 4. check-loa.sh ------------------------------------------------------------
+OUT="$WORK/check-loa.out"
+rc=0
+(cd "$DOWN" && CI=true bash .claude/scripts/check-loa.sh < /dev/null) > "$OUT" 2>&1 || rc=$?
+echo "----- check-loa.sh (downstream) -----"
+cat "$OUT"
+echo "----- end check-loa.sh (exit $rc) -----"
+
+tampered=$(grep -c 'Tampered: ' "$OUT" || true)
+missing=$(grep -c 'Missing: ' "$OUT" || true)
+not_mounted=$(sed -n 's/.*not-mounted: \([0-9][0-9]*\) path(s).*/\1/p' "$OUT")
+echo "fresh-mount-proof: Tampered=${tampered} Missing=${missing} not-mounted=${not_mounted:-0} check-loa-rc=${rc}"
+[[ $rc -eq 0 ]] && exit 0
+exit 1

@@ -0,0 +1,168 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# tools/gen-checksums.sh — cycle-130 FR-1 (#1267; SDD §5.1, DEC-0368)
+#
+# Writes the System Zone integrity manifest `.claude/checksums.json` from the
+# TRACKED `.claude/` tree only. The legacy generators (mount-loa.sh and
+# update.sh `generate_checksums`) walk the working tree with `find`, so build,
+# cache and runtime artefacts (`__pycache__`, `.pytest_cache`, `node_modules`,
+# `.run/`) that exist only on the generating machine end up in the manifest and
+# read as Missing on every fresh mount. This generator lists
+#
+#   git -C ROOT ls-files -z -- .claude
+#
+# minus every path under `.claude/overrides/` (user-owned) and minus the
+# manifest itself (`.claude/checksums.json`), hashes each with
+# `sha256_portable` (.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh) and writes
+#
+#   {"generated": "<UTC ISO-8601>", "algorithm": "sha256",
+#    "files": {"<path>": "<sha256 hex>", ...}}
+#
+# pretty-printed by jq (2-space), keys in `LC_ALL=C` byte order. Two runs on
+# the same tree are byte-identical except `generated`. The working-tree content
+# of each tracked path is hashed (an unstaged edit is reflected); a tracked
+# path deleted from the working tree is skipped with a warning on stderr.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   tools/gen-checksums.sh [--root DIR] [--out FILE]   # (re)generate
+#   tools/gen-checksums.sh --check [--root DIR] [--out FILE]
+#
+# Options:
+#   --root DIR   repository work tree to read (default: the git top level of
+#                the current directory)
+#   --out FILE   manifest path (default: ROOT/.claude/checksums.json). With
+#                --check this is the committed manifest that is compared.
+#   --check      regenerate to a temp file and compare its `files` map with
+#                the manifest at --out; nothing is written
+#   -h, --help   this text
+#
+# Exit codes:
+#   0  generated, or --check: the `files` maps are identical
+#   1  --check: drift (the first ten differing paths, each labelled added /
+#      removed / changed, on stderr) or the manifest is absent / not JSON
+#   2  usage error, ROOT is not a git work tree, or a tracked path name that
+#      cannot be represented safely (newline, tab or backslash)
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+export LC_ALL=C
+
+SELF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
+# shellcheck source=../.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh
+source "${SELF_DIR}/../.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"
+
+usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# =====/p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed -e '$d' -e 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
+die2() { echo "gen-checksums: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
+
+MANIFEST_REL=".claude/checksums.json"
+ROOT=""
+OUT=""
+CHECK=0
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --check) CHECK=1; shift ;;
+    --root)
+      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--root requires a directory"
+      ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --out)
+      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--out requires a file path"
+      OUT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
+    *) die2 "unknown argument: $1 (see --help)" ;;
+  esac
+done
+
+if [[ -z "$ROOT" ]]; then
+  ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die2 "not inside a git work tree (use --root DIR)"
+fi
+[[ -d "$ROOT" ]] || die2 "--root is not a directory: $ROOT"
+ROOT="$(cd "$ROOT" && pwd -P)"
+[[ "$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree 2>/dev/null || true)" == "true" ]] \
+  || die2 "not a git work tree: $ROOT"
+[[ -n "$OUT" ]] || OUT="${ROOT}/${MANIFEST_REL}"
+
+TMP_DIR="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gen-checksums.XXXXXX")"
+cleanup() { rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"; }
+trap cleanup EXIT
+
+# --- 1. the tracked set (NUL-safe, C-sorted, overrides and manifest removed) --
+files=()
+while IFS= read -r -d '' path; do
+  case "$path" in
+    .claude/overrides/*|"$MANIFEST_REL") continue ;;
+  esac
+  case "$path" in
+    *$'\n'*|*$'\t'*|*\\*) die2 "refusing a tracked path with a newline, tab or backslash: $(printf '%q' "$path")" ;;
+  esac
+  if [[ ! -f "${ROOT}/${path}" ]]; then
+    # A gitlink, a dangling symlink or a path deleted in the working tree.
+    echo "gen-checksums: warning: tracked path not a file in the working tree, skipped: $path" >&2
+    continue
+  fi
+  files+=("$path")
+done < <(git -C "$ROOT" ls-files -z -- .claude | sort -z)
+
+# --- 2. hash in chunks (one sha256 process per 400 paths, order preserved) ----
+TSV="${TMP_DIR}/files.tsv"
+: > "$TSV"
+n=${#files[@]}
+i=0
+while [[ $i -lt $n ]]; do
+  chunk=("${files[@]:i:400}")
+  hashes=()
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    hashes+=("${line%% *}")
+  done < <(cd "$ROOT" && sha256_portable "${chunk[@]}")
+  [[ ${#hashes[@]} -eq ${#chunk[@]} ]] || die2 "sha256 returned ${#hashes[@]} digests for ${#chunk[@]} paths"
+  j=0
+  while [[ $j -lt ${#chunk[@]} ]]; do
+    [[ "${hashes[j]}" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || die2 "unexpected sha256 output for ${chunk[j]}"
+    printf '%s\t%s\n' "${chunk[j]}" "${hashes[j]}" >> "$TSV"
+    j=$((j + 1))
+  done
+  i=$((i + 400))
+done
+[[ $n -gt 0 ]] || echo "gen-checksums: warning: no tracked files under .claude in $ROOT" >&2
+
+GEN="${TMP_DIR}/checksums.json"
+jq -Rn --arg generated "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" '
+  {generated: $generated, algorithm: "sha256",
+   files: ([inputs | select(length > 0) | split("\t") | {key: .[0], value: .[1]}] | from_entries)}
+' < "$TSV" > "$GEN"
+
+# --- 3a. write ----------------------------------------------------------------
+if [[ $CHECK -eq 0 ]]; then
+  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
+  chmod 0644 "$GEN"
+  # mv replaces a symlinked manifest instead of writing through it.
+  mv -f "$GEN" "$OUT"
+  echo "gen-checksums: wrote $n entries to $OUT" >&2
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+# --- 3b. --check --------------------------------------------------------------
+if [[ ! -f "$OUT" ]]; then
+  echo "gen-checksums: --check: manifest not found: $OUT (run tools/gen-checksums.sh)" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+if ! jq -e '.files | type == "object"' "$OUT" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  echo "gen-checksums: --check: manifest is not JSON with a files object: $OUT" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+DIFF="${TMP_DIR}/diff.txt"
+jq -rn --slurpfile old "$OUT" --slurpfile new "$GEN" '
+  ($old[0].files) as $o | ($new[0].files) as $n |
+  ( [ $n | keys[] | . as $p | select($o | has($p) | not) | {p: $p, k: "added"} ]
+  + [ $o | keys[] | . as $p | select($n | has($p) | not) | {p: $p, k: "removed"} ]
+  + [ $n | keys[] | . as $p | select(($o | has($p)) and $o[$p] != $n[$p]) | {p: $p, k: "changed"} ] )
+  | sort_by(.p) | .[] | "\(.k): \(.p)"
+' > "$DIFF"
+count=$(wc -l < "$DIFF" | tr -d ' ')
+if [[ "$count" -eq 0 ]]; then
+  echo "gen-checksums: --check: OK ($n entries match $OUT)" >&2
+  exit 0
+fi
+echo "gen-checksums: --check: DRIFT — $count path(s) differ between $OUT and the tracked tree:" >&2
+sed -n '1,10s/^/  /p' "$DIFF" >&2
+[[ "$count" -le 10 ]] || echo "  ... and $((count - 10)) more" >&2
+echo "gen-checksums: regenerate with: bash tools/gen-checksums.sh" >&2
+exit 1

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# tools/check-manifest-paths.sh — cycle-130 FR-1 (#1267; SDD §5.2, DEC-0368)
+#
+# CI gate for the System Zone integrity manifest: every path listed in
+# `.claude/checksums.json` must be TRACKED (`git ls-files -- .claude`) and
+# PRESENT in the working tree. A manifest generated by walking a dirty tree
+# (the #1267 class) lists build, cache and runtime artefacts that no fresh
+# mount has, so every downstream `check-loa.sh` reports them as Missing.
+#
+# Offenders are grouped on stderr:
+#   untracked  — listed in the manifest, not in `git ls-files`; each carries a
+#                DIAGNOSTIC class (first match wins):
+#                  __pycache__ | .pytest_cache | node_modules | .run
+#                      (a path component of that name)
+#                  .pyc   (name ends in .pyc)
+#                  .lock  (name ends in .lock)
+#                  other
+#   missing    — tracked, but absent from the working tree
+# The classes label untracked offenders only: a TRACKED path is never flagged
+# for its name (a committed `.lock` fixture is legitimate).
+#
+# Last line on stdout:
+#   manifest-paths: N entries, M untracked (class=count, ...), K missing
+#
+# Usage:
+#   tools/check-manifest-paths.sh [--manifest FILE] [--root DIR]
+#
+# Options:
+#   --root DIR       repository work tree (default: the git top level of the
+#                    current directory)
+#   --manifest FILE  manifest to check (default: ROOT/.claude/checksums.json)
+#   -h, --help       this text
+#
+# Exit codes:
+#   0  every manifest path is tracked and present
+#   1  at least one untracked or missing path (listed on stderr)
+#   2  usage error, ROOT is not a git work tree, or the manifest is absent or
+#      not JSON with a `files` object
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+export LC_ALL=C
+
+usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# =====/p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed -e '$d' -e 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
+die2() { echo "check-manifest-paths: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
+
+ROOT=""
+MANIFEST=""
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --root)
+      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--root requires a directory"
+      ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --manifest)
+      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--manifest requires a file path"
+      MANIFEST="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
+    *) die2 "unknown argument: $1 (see --help)" ;;
+  esac
+done
+
+if [[ -z "$ROOT" ]]; then
+  ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die2 "not inside a git work tree (use --root DIR)"
+fi
+[[ -d "$ROOT" ]] || die2 "--root is not a directory: $ROOT"
+ROOT="$(cd "$ROOT" && pwd -P)"
+[[ "$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree 2>/dev/null || true)" == "true" ]] \
+  || die2 "not a git work tree: $ROOT"
+[[ -n "$MANIFEST" ]] || MANIFEST="${ROOT}/.claude/checksums.json"
+[[ -f "$MANIFEST" ]] || die2 "manifest not found: $MANIFEST"
+jq -e '.files | type == "object"' "$MANIFEST" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
+  || die2 "manifest is not JSON with a files object: $MANIFEST"
+
+TMP_DIR="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/check-manifest-paths.XXXXXX")"
+cleanup() { rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"; }
+trap cleanup EXIT
+
+# Both lists newline-separated and C-sorted. A path with a newline cannot be
+# represented in either list; gen-checksums.sh refuses to emit one.
+git -C "$ROOT" ls-files -- .claude | sort -u > "${TMP_DIR}/tracked"
+jq -r '.files | keys[]' "$MANIFEST" | sort -u > "${TMP_DIR}/listed"
+comm -23 "${TMP_DIR}/listed" "${TMP_DIR}/tracked" > "${TMP_DIR}/untracked"
+comm -12 "${TMP_DIR}/listed" "${TMP_DIR}/tracked" > "${TMP_DIR}/both"
+
+classify() {
+  local p="$1"
+  if [[ "$p" =~ (^|/)(__pycache__|\.pytest_cache|node_modules|\.run)(/|$) ]]; then
+    printf '%s' "${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
+  elif [[ "$p" == *.pyc ]]; then
+    printf '.pyc'
+  elif [[ "$p" == *.lock ]]; then
+    printf '.lock'
+  else
+    printf 'other'
+  fi
+}
+
+# Classified untracked offenders: "<class>\t<path>"
+: > "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls"
+while IFS= read -r p; do
+  [[ -n "$p" ]] || continue
+  printf '%s\t%s\n' "$(classify "$p")" "$p" >> "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls"
+done < "${TMP_DIR}/untracked"
+
+: > "${TMP_DIR}/missing"
+while IFS= read -r p; do
+  [[ -n "$p" ]] || continue
+  [[ -e "${ROOT}/${p}" ]] || printf '%s\n' "$p" >> "${TMP_DIR}/missing"
+done < "${TMP_DIR}/both"
+
+entries=$(wc -l < "${TMP_DIR}/listed" | tr -d ' ')
+n_untracked=$(wc -l < "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls" | tr -d ' ')
+n_missing=$(wc -l < "${TMP_DIR}/missing" | tr -d ' ')
+
+class_summary=""
+if [[ "$n_untracked" -gt 0 ]]; then
+  echo "check-manifest-paths: untracked manifest paths (not in git ls-files -- .claude), by class:" >&2
+  for cls in __pycache__ .pytest_cache node_modules .run .pyc .lock other; do
+    c=$(awk -F'\t' -v c="$cls" '$1 == c' "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
+    [[ "$c" -gt 0 ]] || continue
+    class_summary="${class_summary:+${class_summary}, }${cls}=${c}"
+    echo "  [${cls}] ${c} path(s):" >&2
+    awk -F'\t' -v c="$cls" '$1 == c { print "    " $2 }' "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls" >&2
+  done
+fi
+if [[ "$n_missing" -gt 0 ]]; then
+  echo "check-manifest-paths: tracked manifest paths absent from the working tree:" >&2
+  sed 's/^/    /' "${TMP_DIR}/missing" >&2
+fi
+
+echo "manifest-paths: ${entries} entries, ${n_untracked} untracked${class_summary:+ (${class_summary})}, ${n_missing} missing"
+if [[ "$n_untracked" -gt 0 || "$n_missing" -gt 0 ]]; then
+  echo "check-manifest-paths: FAIL — regenerate with: bash tools/gen-checksums.sh" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+exit 0

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh — cycle-130 FR-1 (#1267; SDD §5.4, AC-1.3)
+#
+# Proves that a FRESH downstream submodule mount of this repository passes
+# `check-loa.sh` integrity: no Tampered, no Missing (paths the mount does not
+# link by design are reported as not-mounted and do not fail).
+#
+# Steps, all inside a new temp directory (nothing outside it is written):
+#   1. upstream/   — a `git clone` of this repository over file://, with a
+#                    local branch `fresh-mount-proof` at REF. With --worktree
+#                    the source work tree's uncommitted state (tracked edits,
+#                    deletions and untracked non-ignored files) is copied in
+#                    and committed on that branch, inside the temp clone only.
+#   2. downstream/ — `git init`, one commit, then the downstream entry point
+#                    `upstream/.claude/scripts/mount-submodule.sh --branch
+#                    fresh-mount-proof --ref <sha> --force` with
+#                    LOA_UPSTREAM=file://.../upstream (the mount clones the
+#                    submodule from there; no network).
+#   3. `aleph.enabled: false` is set in downstream/.loa.config.yaml.
+#   4. `bash .claude/scripts/check-loa.sh` runs in downstream/; its full output
+#      is printed, then a summary line
+#        fresh-mount-proof: Tampered=T Missing=M not-mounted=N check-loa-rc=R
+#
+# Git runs hermetically: GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1,
+# a fixed identity, protocol.file.allow=always (needed for a file:// submodule
+# on git >= 2.38.1) and core.hooksPath pointed at an empty directory.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh [--ref REF] [--worktree] [--keep] [--tmp DIR]
+#
+# Options:
+#   --ref REF    commit-ish of this repository to mount (default: HEAD of the
+#                repository the script lives in)
+#   --worktree   mount REF plus the source work tree's uncommitted state
+#                (use before the change is committed)
+#   --keep       keep the temp directory and print its path
+#   --tmp DIR    parent directory for the temp directory (default: $TMPDIR or
+#                /tmp)
+#   -h, --help   this text
+#
+# Exit codes:
+#   0    check-loa.sh exited 0 on the fresh mount
+#   1    check-loa.sh exited non-zero (its output names the failures)
+#   2    usage error
+#   3    setup failed (clone, overlay, downstream init or the mount itself);
+#        the failing step's output is printed
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+export LC_ALL=C
+
+usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# =====/p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed -e '$d' -e 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
+die2() { echo "fresh-mount-proof: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
+die3() { echo "fresh-mount-proof: SETUP FAILED: $*" >&2; exit 3; }
+
+REF=""
+KEEP=0
+WORKTREE=0
+TMP_PARENT="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}"
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --ref)
+      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--ref requires a commit-ish"
+      REF="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --tmp)
+      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--tmp requires a directory"
+      TMP_PARENT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --keep) KEEP=1; shift ;;
+    --worktree) WORKTREE=1; shift ;;
+    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
+    *) die2 "unknown argument: $1 (see --help)" ;;

+WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMP_PARENT%/}/fresh-mount-proof.XXXXXX")"
+cleanup() {
+  if [[ $KEEP -eq 1 ]]; then
+    echo "fresh-mount-proof: kept $WORK" >&2
+  else
+    rm -rf "$WORK"
+  fi
+}
+trap cleanup EXIT
+
+# --- hermetic git ---------------------------------------------------------------
+mkdir -p "$WORK/no-hooks"
+export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1
+export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=3
+export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=protocol.file.allow GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=always
+export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1=core.hooksPath GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1="$WORK/no-hooks"
+export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_2=init.defaultBranch GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_2=main
+export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="fresh-mount-proof" GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="fresh-mount-proof@localhost"
+export GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="$GIT_AUTHOR_NAME" GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="$GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL"
+unset LOA_ALEPH_ENABLED
+

+run_step() {  # run_step <description> <cmd...>; output to $LOG, printed on failure
+  local desc="$1"; shift

+    cat "$LOG" >&2
+    die3 "$desc"

+[[ $WORKTREE -eq 1 ]] && suffix=" + work-tree state"
+echo "fresh-mount-proof: source $SRC at ${REF_SHA}${suffix}"
+echo "fresh-mount-proof: temp dir $WORK"

+run_step "clone $SRC" git clone --quiet --no-checkout "file://$SRC" "$UP"
+run_step "fetch $REF_SHA" git -C "$UP" fetch --quiet origin "$REF_SHA"
+run_step "branch at $REF_SHA" git -C "$UP" checkout --quiet -B fresh-mount-proof "$REF_SHA"
+

+  local p
+  while IFS= read -r -d '' p; do
+    if [[ -e "$SRC/$p" || -L "$SRC/$p" ]]; then
+      [[ -d "$SRC/$p" && ! -L "$SRC/$p" ]] && continue   # gitlink / nested repo
+      mkdir -p "$UP/$(dirname "$p")"
+      rm -f "$UP/$p"
+      cp -P "$SRC/$p" "$UP/$p"
+    else
+      rm -f "$UP/$p"
+    fi
+  done < <(git -C "$SRC" ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard)

+  git -C "$UP" commit --quiet --allow-empty -m "fresh-mount-proof: work-tree state of $SRC"

+  git -C "$DOWN" commit --quiet -m "initial commit"

+    --branch fresh-mount-proof --ref "$MOUNT_SHA" --force < /dev/null)

+# --- 3. Aleph off ---------------------------------------------------------------

+else

+cat "$OUT"
+echo "----- end check-loa.sh (exit $rc) -----"
+

+missing=$(grep -c 'Missing: ' "$OUT" || true)
+not_mounted=$(sed -n 's/.*not-mounted: \([0-9][0-9]*\) path(s).*/\1/p' "$OUT")
+echo "fresh-mount-proof: Tampered=${tampered} Missing=${missing} not-mounted=${not_mounted:-0} check-loa-rc=${rc}"
+[[ $rc -eq 0 ]] && exit 0
+exit 1

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# tools/gen-checksums.sh — cycle-130 FR-1 (#1267; SDD §5.1, DEC-0368)
+#
+# Writes the System Zone integrity manifest `.claude/checksums.json` from the
+# TRACKED `.claude/` tree only. The legacy generators (mount-loa.sh and
+# update.sh `generate_checksums`) walk the working tree with `find`, so build,
+# cache and runtime artefacts (`__pycache__`, `.pytest_cache`, `node_modules`,
+# `.run/`) that exist only on the generating machine end up in the manifest and
+# read as Missing on every fresh mount. This generator lists
+#
+#   git -C ROOT ls-files -z -- .claude
+#
+# minus every path under `.claude/overrides/` (user-owned) and minus the
+# manifest itself (`.claude/checksums.json`), hashes each with
+# `sha256_portable` (.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh) and writes
+#
+#   {"generated": "<UTC ISO-8601>", "algorithm": "sha256",
+#    "files": {"<path>": "<sha256 hex>", ...}}
+#
+# pretty-printed by jq (2-space), keys in `LC_ALL=C` byte order. Two runs on
+# the same tree are byte-identical except `generated`. The working-tree content
+# of each tracked path is hashed (an unstaged edit is reflected); a tracked
+# path deleted from the working tree is skipped with a warning on stderr.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   tools/gen-checksums.sh [--root DIR] [--out FILE]   # (re)generate
+#   tools/gen-checksums.sh --check [--root DIR] [--out FILE]
+#
+# Options:
+#   --root DIR   repository work tree to read (default: the git top level of
+#                the current directory)
+#   --out FILE   manifest path (default: ROOT/.claude/checksums.json). With
+#                --check this is the committed manifest that is compared.
+#   --check      regenerate to a temp file and compare its `files` map with
+#                the manifest at --out; nothing is written
+#   -h, --help   this text
+#
+# Exit codes:
+#   0  generated, or --check: the `files` maps are identical
+#   1  --check: drift (the first ten differing paths, each labelled added /
+#      removed / changed, on stderr) or the manifest is absent / not JSON
+#   2  usage error, ROOT is not a git work tree, or a tracked path name that
+#      cannot be represented safely (newline, tab or backslash)
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+export LC_ALL=C
+
+SELF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
+# shellcheck source=../.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh
+source "${SELF_DIR}/../.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"
+
+usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# =====/p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed -e '$d' -e 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
+die2() { echo "gen-checksums: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
+
+MANIFEST_REL=".claude/checksums.json"
+ROOT=""
+OUT=""
+CHECK=0
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --check) CHECK=1; shift ;;
+    --root)
+      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--root requires a directory"
+      ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --out)
+      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--out requires a file path"
+      OUT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
+    *) die2 "unknown argument: $1 (see --help)" ;;
+  esac
+done
+
+if [[ -z "$ROOT" ]]; then
+  ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die2 "not inside a git work tree (use --root DIR)"
+fi
+[[ -d "$ROOT" ]] || die2 "--root is not a directory: $ROOT"
+ROOT="$(cd "$ROOT" && pwd -P)"
+[[ "$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree 2>/dev/null || true)" == "true" ]] \
+  || die2 "not a git work tree: $ROOT"
+[[ -n "$OUT" ]] || OUT="${ROOT}/${MANIFEST_REL}"
+
+TMP_DIR="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gen-checksums.XXXXXX")"
+cleanup() { rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"; }
+trap cleanup EXIT
+
+# --- 1. the tracked set (NUL-safe, C-sorted, overrides and manifest removed) --
+files=()
+while IFS= read -r -d '' path; do
+  case "$path" in
+    .claude/overrides/*|"$MANIFEST_REL") continue ;;
+  esac
+  case "$path" in
+    *$'\n'*|*$'\t'*|*\\*) die2 "refusing a tracked path with a newline, tab or backslash: $(printf '%q' "$path")" ;;
+  esac
+  if [[ ! -f "${ROOT}/${path}" ]]; then
+    # A gitlink, a dangling symlink or a path deleted in the working tree.
+    echo "gen-checksums: warning: tracked path not a file in the working tree, skipped: $path" >&2
+    continue
+  fi
+  files+=("$path")
+done < <(git -C "$ROOT" ls-files -z -- .claude | sort -z)
+
+# --- 2. hash in chunks (one sha256 process per 400 paths, order preserved) ----
+TSV="${TMP_DIR}/files.tsv"
+: > "$TSV"
+n=${#files[@]}
+i=0
+while [[ $i -lt $n ]]; do
+  chunk=("${files[@]:i:400}")
+  hashes=()
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    hashes+=("${line%% *}")
+  done < <(cd "$ROOT" && sha256_portable "${chunk[@]}")
+  [[ ${#hashes[@]} -eq ${#chunk[@]} ]] || die2 "sha256 returned ${#hashes[@]} digests for ${#chunk[@]} paths"
+  j=0
+  while [[ $j -lt ${#chunk[@]} ]]; do
+    [[ "${hashes[j]}" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || die2 "unexpected sha256 output for ${chunk[j]}"
+    printf '%s\t%s\n' "${chunk[j]}" "${hashes[j]}" >> "$TSV"
+    j=$((j + 1))
+  done
+  i=$((i + 400))
+done
+[[ $n -gt 0 ]] || echo "gen-checksums: warning: no tracked files under .claude in $ROOT" >&2
+
+GEN="${TMP_DIR}/checksums.json"
+jq -Rn --arg generated "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" '
+  {generated: $generated, algorithm: "sha256",
+   files: ([inputs | select(length > 0) | split("\t") | {key: .[0], value: .[1]}] | from_entries)}
+' < "$TSV" > "$GEN"
+
+# --- 3a. write ----------------------------------------------------------------
+if [[ $CHECK -eq 0 ]]; then
+  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
+  chmod 0644 "$GEN"
+  # mv replaces a symlinked manifest instead of writing through it.
+  mv -f "$GEN" "$OUT"
+  echo "gen-checksums: wrote $n entries to $OUT" >&2
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+# --- 3b. --check --------------------------------------------------------------
+if [[ ! -f "$OUT" ]]; then
+  echo "gen-checksums: --check: manifest not found: $OUT (run tools/gen-checksums.sh)" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+if ! jq -e '.files | type == "object"' "$OUT" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  echo "gen-checksums: --check: manifest is not JSON with a files object: $OUT" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+DIFF="${TMP_DIR}/diff.txt"
+jq -rn --slurpfile old "$OUT" --slurpfile new "$GEN" '
+  ($old[0].files) as $o | ($new[0].files) as $n |
+  ( [ $n | keys[] | . as $p | select($o | has($p) | not) | {p: $p, k: "added"} ]
+  + [ $o | keys[] | . as $p | select($n | has($p) | not) | {p: $p, k: "removed"} ]
+  + [ $n | keys[] | . as $p | select(($o | has($p)) and $o[$p] != $n[$p]) | {p: $p, k: "changed"} ] )
+  | sort_by(.p) | .[] | "\(.k): \(.p)"
+' > "$DIFF"
+count=$(wc -l < "$DIFF" | tr -d ' ')
+if [[ "$count" -eq 0 ]]; then
+  echo "gen-checksums: --check: OK ($n entries match $OUT)" >&2
+  exit 0
+fi
+echo "gen-checksums: --check: DRIFT — $count path(s) differ between $OUT and the tracked tree:" >&2
+sed -n '1,10s/^/  /p' "$DIFF" >&2
+[[ "$count" -le 10 ]] || echo "  ... and $((count - 10)) more" >&2
+echo "gen-checksums: regenerate with: bash tools/gen-checksums.sh" >&2
+exit 1

+# The prompt tree as the pipeline mounts it: a catalog with two default_effort

+extend_tree() {
+  mkdir -p "$PT/.claude/defaults" "$PT/.claude/skills/implementing-tasks" "$PT/.claude/scripts/beads" "$PT/.claude/overrides"

+# check-loa.sh's own integrity check, run inside the sandbox (its cwd-relative manifest)
+integrity_in() {

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# claude-ablation-stub.sh — wraps evals/tests/fixtures/claude-stub.sh for the
+# cycle-130 bats (run-arms.bats, arm-toggles.bats). No model call.
+#

+#   STUB_CONC_DIR      concurrency probe: each call registers itself in the dir
+#                      for STUB_SLEEP seconds and appends the number of calls
+#                      running at its start to <dir>.log

+  : > "$STUB_CONC_DIR/$$"
+  ls "$STUB_CONC_DIR" | wc -l | tr -d ' ' >> "$STUB_CONC_DIR.log"

+# suite-lib.bash — fixture-suite builders for validate-suite.bats and freeze.bats
+# (cycle-130 Sprint 258 Task 1.11). Sourced by the bats files; the templates are
+# the two committed smoke tasks, so the fixtures follow the real schema.
+#
+#   make_task <root> <group> <id> <type>   copy a smoke task to <root>/<group>/<id>
+#                                          as <type> (build types from smoke-build-01,
+#                                          review-catch from smoke-review-01)
+#   make_full_suite <root>                 four tasks of each type under tasks/
+
+SMOKE_ROOT="${SMOKE_ROOT:-$REPO_ROOT/grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/smoke}"
+
+make_task() {
+  local root="$1" group="$2" id="$3" type="$4" src
+  case "$type" in review-catch) src="$SMOKE_ROOT/smoke-review-01" ;; *) src="$SMOKE_ROOT/smoke-build-01" ;; esac
+  mkdir -p "$root/$group"
+  cp -a "$src" "$root/$group/$id"
+  local ty="$root/$group/$id/task.yaml"
+  ID="$id" TY="$type" yq -i '.id = strenv(ID) | .type = strenv(TY)' "$ty"
+  if [[ "$type" != "review-catch" ]]; then
+    FX="$group/$id/fixture" yq -i '.fixture = strenv(FX)' "$ty"
+  fi
+  if [[ "$type" == "refactor" ]]; then
+    printf 'def test_structure():\n    assert True\n' > "$root/$group/$id/hidden/tests/test_structure_check.py"
+    yq -i '.structural_check = "hidden/tests/test_structure_check.py"' "$ty"
+  fi
+}
+
+make_full_suite() {
+  local root="$1" ty i
+  for ty in feature-build bug-fix refactor review-catch; do
+    for i in 1 2 3 4; do make_task "$root" tasks "$ty-0$i" "$ty"; done
+  done
+}

+# line (`# Phase: <NAME>`); the stub records what the executor gave it and emits a
+# stream-json transcript with a system/init event (session_id), per-turn
+# assistant events carrying usage, and a result event.
+#   STUB_LOG_DIR            per call: call-<n>.argv (NUL-separated), call-<n>.env
+#                           (`env` output), call-<n>.fds (ls /proc/self/fd), call-<n>.phase,
+#                           call-<n>.pwd. The executor's `env -i` strips these
+#                           controls, so tests reach the stub through a wrapper that
+#                           records pending.env / pending.fds and then loads them.
+#   STUB_COST_<PHASE>       result total_cost_usd (default 0.5)
+#   STUB_TURNS_<PHASE>      assistant turns to emit (default 2)
+#   STUB_TURN_OUT_<PHASE>   output tokens per turn (default 100)
+#   STUB_TURN_SLEEP         seconds between turns (default 0)
+#   STUB_SLEEP_<PHASE>      seconds to sleep before the result event

+#   STUB_MODEL_USED_<PHASE> model id reported in modelUsage (default: --model)
+#   STUB_REFUSAL_<PHASE>    1: emit a system/model_refusal_fallback event
+#   STUB_DOT_CLAUDE_WRITE_<PHASE>  1: emit a Write tool_use under .claude/

+#                           calling_primitive / effort / effort_effective come from
+#                           STUB_PRIMITIVE_<PHASE>, STUB_HOP_EFFORT_<PHASE>,
+#                           STUB_HOP_EFFECTIVE_<PHASE>
+set -euo pipefail
+if [[ "${1:-}" == "--version" ]]; then echo "2.1.299 (Claude Code) stub"; exit 0; fi

+args=("$@")
+i=0
+while [[ $i -lt ${#args[@]} ]]; do
+  case "${args[$i]}" in
+    -p) prompt="${args[$((i + 1))]}"; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+    --model) model="${args[$((i + 1))]}"; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+    --resume) resume="${args[$((i + 1))]}"; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+  esac
+  i=$((i + 1))

+  mkdir -p "$STUB_LOG_DIR"
+  n=1; while [[ -e "$STUB_LOG_DIR/call-$n.argv" ]]; do n=$((n + 1)); done
+  printf '%s\0' "$@" > "$STUB_LOG_DIR/call-$n.argv"

+  if [[ -f "$STUB_LOG_DIR/pending.env" ]]; then mv "$STUB_LOG_DIR/pending.env" "$STUB_LOG_DIR/call-$n.env"
+  else env | sed -E 's/^(AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK)=.*/\1=<set>/' > "$STUB_LOG_DIR/call-$n.env"; fi   # key name only
+  if [[ -f "$STUB_LOG_DIR/pending.fds" ]]; then mv "$STUB_LOG_DIR/pending.fds" "$STUB_LOG_DIR/call-$n.fds"

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats — cycle-130 Sprint 258 Tasks 1.7 + 1.12
+# (SDD §1.4 D-4.1 … D-4.10, §5.6; sprint.md AC-1.7, AC-1.12, AC-1.14; PRD AC-4.x)
+#
+# evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh drives Loa's phases as separate CLI sessions in a
+# sandbox repository. Here the CLI is evals/tests/fixtures/claude-stub-pipeline.sh,
+# docker is fixtures/docker-stub.sh, and the executor runs from a temporary copy of
+# the harness (make_harness) whose lib/sandbox-mount.sh is fixtures/mount-lib-stub.sh:
+# the shipped script sources its library by a literal path only (eval.yml trust
+# boundary), so there is no environment override to point. The executor runs the CLI under
+# `env -i`, which strips the stubs' control variables, so each test reaches the
+# stubs through generated wrappers ($T/claude, $T/docker) that first record the
+# environment and descriptors the executor gave them, then load $T/stub.env.
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
+  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
+  FP="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/fingerprint.sh"
+  STUB="$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/claude-stub-pipeline.sh"
+  DSTUB="$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/docker-stub.sh"
+  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/pr.XXXXXX")"
+  export LOA_EVAL_WATCHDOG_POLL_S=0.1
+  export LOA_EVAL_PRICING_JSON='{"global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5":{"input_per_mtok":4000000,"output_per_mtok":20000000},"global.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1":{"input_per_mtok":10000000,"output_per_mtok":50000000}}'
+  export LOA_EVAL_CREDS_HOME="$T/home"
+  : > "$T/stub.env"
+  make_harness
+  make_source_tree
+  cp "$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/ablation-runs/suite.yaml" "$T/suite.yaml"   # B's suite file as landed
+  make_tasks
+  make_wrappers
+}
+
+teardown() {
+  chmod -R u+rwx "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
+  find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
+  rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
+}
+
+make_source_tree() {
+  local s
+  mkdir -p "$T/src/.claude/loa" "$T/src/.claude/scripts"
+  for s in planning-sprints implementing-tasks reviewing-code auditing-security; do
+    mkdir -p "$T/src/.claude/skills/$s"
+    printf -- '---\nname: %s\neffort: xhigh\n---\nbody\n' "$s" > "$T/src/.claude/skills/$s/SKILL.md"
+  done
+  echo "loa" > "$T/src/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+  printf 'flatline_protocol:\n  enabled: true\n  code_review:\n    enabled: true\n  security_audit:\n    enabled: true\n' > "$T/src/.loa.config.yaml"
+  ( cd "$T/src" && git init -q && git add -A && git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit -qm init )
+  # the operator's credential directories (copied per run in container mode)
+  mkdir -p "$T/home/.aws" "$T/home/.claude/projects/big" "$T/home/.codex/sessions"
+  echo "[default]" > "$T/home/.aws/config"
+  echo "{}" > "$T/home/.claude/settings.json"
+  echo "history" > "$T/home/.claude/history.jsonl"
+  echo "{}" > "$T/home/.codex/auth.json"
+  echo "model = 'x'" > "$T/home/.codex/config.toml"
+  echo '{"claudeAiOauth": "subscription"}' > "$T/home/.claude/.credentials.json"
+}
+
+# a temporary copy of the harness: the stub mount library sits at the literal path
+# pipeline-run.sh sources (lib/sandbox-mount.sh)
+make_harness() {
+  H="$T/h/evals/harness"
+  mkdir -p "$H/lib"
+  cp "$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh" "$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/fingerprint.sh" "$H/"
+  cp -a "$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/lib/phase-prompts" "$H/lib/"
+  cp "$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/mount-lib-stub.sh" "$H/lib/sandbox-mount.sh"
+  PR="$H/pipeline-run.sh"
+}
+
+make_tasks() {
+  # build task: fixture tree beside a sibling hidden/ directory that must never be copied
+  local b="$T/suite/tasks/bf-01" r="$T/suite/tasks/rc-01" p="$T/prs/pr-x"
+  mkdir -p "$b/fx/src" "$b/hidden/tests"
+  echo 'print(1)' > "$b/fx/src/app.py"
+  echo 'assert False' > "$b/hidden/tests/test_secret.py"
+  printf 'Make the app print two.\n' > "$b/TASK.md"
+  cat > "$b/task.yaml" <<'YAML'
+id: bf-01
+schema_version: 1
+type: bug-fix
+fixture: fx
+criterion: "the app prints two"
+test_command: ["python3", "-m", "pytest", "-q", "tests"]
+YAML
+  # review-catch task: a PR fixture outside the task dir
+  mkdir -p "$p/base/lib" "$p/head/lib" "$r"
+  echo 'a=1' > "$p/base/lib/x.sh"; echo 'a=2' > "$p/head/lib/x.sh"
+  printf -- '--- a/lib/x.sh\n+++ b/lib/x.sh\n@@ -1 +1 @@\n-a=1\n+a=2\n' > "$p/head.diff"
+  printf '# PR\nChange a.\n' > "$p/PR.md"
+  printf '# Review instructions\nReview it.\n' > "$p/REVIEW-INSTRUCTIONS.md"
+  printf '# Audit instructions\nAudit it.\n' > "$p/AUDIT-INSTRUCTIONS.md"
+  printf 'name: pr-x\ndescription: "planted defects live elsewhere"\n' > "$p/fixture.yaml"
+  printf 'Review the pull request in pr/.\n' > "$r/TASK.md"
+  cat > "$r/task.yaml" <<YAML
+id: rc-01
+schema_version: 1
+type: review-catch
+fixture: null
+criterion: "review the change"
+review_catch: {fixture: "$p"}
+YAML
+  BUILD="$b/task.yaml" REVIEWC="$r/task.yaml"
+}
+
+make_wrappers() {
+  mkdir -p "$T/log" "$T/dlog"
+  cat > "$T/claude" <<EOF
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+env | sed -E 's/^(AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK)=.*/\1=<set>/' > "$T/log/pending.env"   # key name only, never the value
+if [[ -n "\${AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK:-}" ]]; then
+  if [[ "\$AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK" == "\$(cat "$T/token" 2>/dev/null)" ]]; then echo match; else echo mismatch; fi >> "$T/log/token.check"
+fi
+ls "/proc/\$\$/fd" > "$T/log/pending.fds" 2>/dev/null || true
+set -a; . "$T/stub.env"; set +a
+export STUB_LOG_DIR="$T/log"
+exec "$STUB" "\$@"
+EOF
+  cat > "$T/docker" <<EOF
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+export DOCKER_STUB_LOG="$T/dlog" DOCKER_STUB_CLAUDE="$T/claude"
+[[ -f "$T/docker.env" ]] && { set -a; . "$T/docker.env"; set +a; }
+exec "$DSTUB" "\$@"
+EOF
+  chmod +x "$T/claude" "$T/docker"
+}
+
+# run_pr <arm> [task-yaml] [extra args…] — host executor unless --executor given
+run_pr() {
+  local arm="$1" task="${2:-$BUILD}"; shift; [[ $# -gt 0 ]] && shift
+  run "$PR" --task-yaml "$task" --arm "$arm" --run-dir "$T/run" --run-id "r-$arm" --trial 1 \
+    --source-tree "$T/src" --suite-file "$T/suite.yaml" --executor host --claude-bin "$T/claude" "$@"
+}
+labels() { jq -r '[.phases[] | .label] | join(",")' "$T/run/meta/pipeline.json"; }
+ran()    { jq -r '[.phases[] | select(.skipped == false) | .label] | join(",")' "$T/run/meta/pipeline.json"; }
+argv_of() { tr '\0' '\n' < "$T/log/call-$1.argv"; }   # argv_of <n>
+call_for() { grep -lx "$1" "$T"/log/call-*.phase | sed -n '1p' | sed 's/.*call-\([0-9]*\)\.phase/\1/'; }
+

+  [ "$(awk '{print $2}' "$M")" = "$(awk '{print $2}' "$M" | LC_ALL=C sort)" ]
